def beadk(ends):

def valid(ends, bead, static_ends, static_beads):
    allE=ends+static_ends

        for b in list(static_beads)+[bead]:

    for i,b in enumerate(list(static_beads)+[bead]):

    return True
def plan(white, grays, target, static_ends, static_beads, cap=400):

    pq=[(0,0,white,tuple(sorted(grays)),[])]; seen={(white,tuple(sorted(grays)))}; pops=0

            key=(P,tuple(sorted(g)))
            if key in seen or nb not in BOK: continue
            if not valid([P]+list(g),nb,static_ends,static_beads): continue
            seen.add(key)
            heapq.heappush(pq,(c+1+abs(nb[0]-target[0])+abs(nb[1]-target[1]),c+1,P,tuple(sorted(g)),path+[('M',P)]))
        for i in range(len(g)):

            if key in seen: continue
            seen.add(key); nb=beadk([gi]+list(ng))
            heapq.heappush(pq,(c+1+abs(nb[0]-target[0])+abs(nb[1]-target[1]),c+1,gi,ng,path+[('S',gi)]))

request_payload_crosscheck.note: Snapshots directly show memory blocks in outgoing request messages, completed-level rule instructions, and exact later tool code/output. Prior-response usage identifies the preceding generated response; it is not an isolated cost of the memory block.

limitations: The helper records observed level transitions separately from unverified model hypotheses.
Final memory summary and delivered-block hashes do not identify which rule was available at which earlier level; actual request timelines are required.
Recaps written after a level completion cannot be used as the cause of that same completion.
Successful-attempt action counts reset on observed RESET; benchmark actions_per_level includes earlier failed attempts and resets.
Total request seconds aggregate concurrent requests and are not GPU elapsed time.
The recorded memory text length is not a tokenizer-measured incremental token cost.
Source hypotheses are actively revised, not all statements in memory are true. Null captured rule does not necessarily mean the model failed to reflect in raw reasoning/code.
All3 candidate payloads and corresponding baseline usage were crosschecked; baseline code/action counterfactuals were not fully reread because this final pass was intentionally lightweight.
Prompt-token differences include changed histories and behavior, not an isolated marginal memory-token estimate. Cache/billing effects are not inferred.

interpretation_of_two_interventions.active_rule_recapping: The post-completion instruction itself changes reasoning on an already scheduled model request; later behavior before a pin refresh can still be consistent with this intervention. It is not excluded for lack of a post-trim header.
interpretation_of_two_interventions.post_trim_system_memory: The helper also reintroduces accumulated facts/hypotheses after history eviction. Transcript blocks match all successful delivery hashes for the three games; concrete later computations/actions are documented.
interpretation_of_two_interventions.separation_limit: No ablation separates recap-only, pin-only, ordinary retained functions, recent history and sampling variation. Evidence supports actual use of earlier mechanics under the combined032 intervention, not causal attribution of every score point to pinned text.

summary_verdict: All three games show concrete later code/action chains using and revising earlier mechanics, beyond header presence or recitation. Observed improvements are compatible with032 combined recap+memory benefit; exact causal share and hidden-score transfer remain unproven. This is an explanatory review, not an additional adoption gate.
